label: FIXED - Les Gets Trappeurs junction n13535054703 was a PHANTOM dip (detector bug, your slope was fine)
note: YOU WERE RIGHT - nothing was wrong with this slope, the DETECTOR was wrong. It reported a 7 m climb-out at n13535054703 @1515 m. The 7 m came entirely from e3141/e3142, a POLYGON SKELETON ARM - a link the app invents for connectivity, not real terrain. The search climbed e3142 (+7 m) to n13535054709 @1522, saw e3141 'descending' from there, and called that the place the descent resumes. But e3141 descends STRAIGHT BACK INTO n13535054703 - it is a loop, not an escape. So the app used its own invention as proof your mountain was broken, while never finding the honest way out: 110 m down e1423 to n13534998799 @1513, on to the Grand Cry station n3232360220 @1513, where Piste des Indiens really does continue down to 1495 m. FIXED GENERICALLY in _phantoms.ts: skeleton arms are excluded from both the escape walk and the resume test, and a resume that returns to the origin is not an escape. FLEET EFFECT: 35 -> 19 pothole sinks, so 16 of 35 were phantom. Nothing to check here - shown only so you can see the arms that caused it.

label: FIXED - D 228 Route des Lindarets n3346682763: 3 m claim was BELOW the noise floor
note: NOTHING TO CHECK - cleared without touching your data. The whole accusation was a 3 m climb-out, but Vmerge (the pipeline's own rule for 'these two heights are the same place, merge them') is 4 m. The detector was firing BELOW the noise floor the builder itself uses, so it flagged a difference buildGraph would have erased. POTHOLE_CLIMB_TOL is now derived from Vmerge instead of being a hard-coded 3, and this node no longer reports. Separately, its OSM tags settled the 'is this a real slope?' question: w327863778 and w420518195 carry piste:type=downhill + piste:difficulty=easy + piste:name (Parchets / Village des Lindarets), and w327863773 adds access:conditional = no @ (Oct-Apr) - cars banned all winter. It is a deliberately mapped winter blue. It LOOKED like a road because normalize.ts preferred the road's `name` over `piste:name`; that is fixed too (143 of 256 such ways fleet-wide were mislabelled), and will show as 'Parchets' after the next data refresh.

label: FIXED - Morzine valley floor n363738232: escape is a builder-certified cat-track
note: NOTHING TO CHECK - cleared without touching your data, and it was the LAST pothole sink in the fleet (now 0 of 18 resorts). Your slope was never the problem. The detector asked 'can a skier get back up out of here?' but answered it with Vmerge (4 m), which is the pipeline's rule for 'are these two points the same place' - a statement about measurement noise, not about a skier. The honest constant is maxTraverseClimb (8 m), which is what buildGraph.ts itself uses to decide whether to give a near-flat run a reverse traverse at all ('more than a skate - that's a real slope'). Measured, the escape from here is +6.7 m over 112 m, a 5.9% net grade - inside both maxTraverseClimb and flatGradeMax, i.e. a two-way cat-track the pipeline had ALREADY certified you can skate back up. All six remaining sinks turned out to be that same thing (ascents 5.0/8.0/6.7/7.0/5.0/7.0 m, grades 3.1/5.6/5.9/4.7/3.1/1.6%). To be sure the check had not just stopped looking, a 15 m sink was injected into a scratch resort and it was still reported - so it fires on a real fault and is simply finding none.

label: FIXED - Les Crosets plaza n1000000000529: cleared by the min-resume fix, never a defect
note: NOTHING TO CHECK. This was reported only because the flat-escape walk used to `break` at the FIRST node offering a descent and report that node's height, so the verdict was decided by edge storage order rather than by the mountain. The walk now takes the LOWEST resume in the whole frontier - a pothole is by definition a dip you can only leave by climbing, so the honest measure is the least climb available. The plaza sits level at 1682-1685 m, exactly as a base area should, and it no longer reports.

label: FIXED - Verbier L'Eteygeon: all 18 were OFF-PISTE, never a connectivity defect
note: NOTHING TO CHECK - cleared without touching your data, and Verbier is now trapped=0 orphan=0 basins=0. All 18 trapped nodes plus both orphans lie on L'Eteygeon / Itineraire Bruson, and EVERY non-off-piste edge in the whole sector is synthetic:true - i.e. rescue/snap connectors the app invented trying to save the itinerary. There is no real piste here to be cut off. A freeride line that descends to the Val de Bagnes floor and stops is not a defect: that is what off-piste IS, and cost.ts refuses those edges entirely unless allowOffPiste is on, so by default a skier cannot even enter this terrain to get stuck in it. Same call already signed off for Tignes' Termignon ('free-ride off-piste, do not add a link'). The bug was that check:trapped and trappedBasins.ts DISAGREED about off-piste: basins has excluded it since the off-piste work, check:trapped never did, so this sector sat on the review list for rounds while check:basins reported it clean. check:trapped now reports off-piste-only nodes separately, exactly like acceptedBasins - the graph is untouched and the BFS is unfiltered. Fleet effect: 48 of 138 trapped and 23 of 57 orphan nodes across 7 resorts were this same class (Verbier 18/18, Tignes 11 -> 1, St Anton 26 -> 15).
